summary: Iteration 7 (bulk CSV/XLSX import for categories & products, category drag-and-drop reorder, per-main-category promo banner, and product-detail full-path breadcrumb) tested end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 pytest tests pass (templates csv+xlsx, category import idempotency, product import path resolution + leaf validation, reorder route ordering & non-shadowing of PUT /categories/{id}, banner persistence). Frontend admin: Import modal opens from both Produits and Catégories tabs with template CSV/XLSX download, file upload and per-row error result; import via UI returned '3 catégories importé(s)'. Category rows expose draggable=true + GripVertical handle. Category form shows Bannière section on level 0 only (confirmed hidden on level 1). 'Bannière' badge appears on row after save. Client /categorie/{id} renders data-testid=category-banner with title & CTA. Product detail page renders data-testid=product-breadcrumb (Accueil > Category > Product).

issues: Native HTML5 drag-drop reorder was NOT emulated in Playwright (native drag events are unreliable to simulate). Verified indirectly: rows have draggable=true, GripVertical handle & 'Glissez-déposez pour réordonner' hint render correctly, and PUT /api/categories/reorder API works via backend tests (order persisted, GET reflects new order, route not shadowed by PUT /categories/{id}).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1583 lines — refactor into routers (auth, catalog, categories, import, admin) is overdue (>700-line guideline).
_read_rows swallows any CSV with a single-column header and retries with semicolon separator (good). But it does NOT catch tab-separated files — consider adding sep sniffing via csv.Sniffer.
_upsert_cat generates slug with 4-hex suffix on collision (fine) but the collision check does not consider deleted-then-recreated categories; acceptable for import scale.
reorder_categories silently skips invalid ObjectId strings — no error is returned for a bad id in the list. Consider returning skipped ids.
import_products stores category_id + category (slug) but leaves subcategory=null; this is consistent with the leaf-only model — fine.
Both import endpoints read entire file in memory (fine at expected CSV sizes, would need streaming for very large imports).

The Bannière badge on the admin row is only shown when banner_image is set; a category with only a title/subtitle configured (no image) will not display the badge — either enforce image required in the form, or make the badge trigger on any banner field.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (drag-drop verified via backend API only)

seed_data_creation: None persisted — all TEST_* categories (TEST_UICat/TEST_UISub/TEST_UILeaf and TEST_ImpMain tree and TEST_BannerMain) and TEST_ImportedProd products were deleted at the end. Verified GET /api/categories still returns 13 mains and no TEST_ leftovers.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 7 feature batch fully working. New endpoints: GET /api/admin/import/template/{categories|products}?format=csv|xlsx (admin, returns downloadable file with UTF-8 BOM for CSV or xlsx zip), POST /api/admin/import/categories (multipart file → {created, errors}, idempotent by label+parent_id), POST /api/admin/import/products (path 'A > B > C' → resolves to leaf category, rows with unresolvable/non-leaf path returned in errors[] with row number = spreadsheet row = index+2), PUT /api/categories/reorder body {ids:[...]} (defined BEFORE PUT /categories/{id} so no shadowing), POST/PUT /api/categories accepts banner_{image,title,subtitle,cta_label,cta_link} which are echoed by GET /api/categories per node. Frontend testids: import-template-csv, import-template-xlsx, import-file-input, import-submit, import-result, admin-import-categories, admin-import-products, admin-cat-{id} (draggable=true), cf-banner-title (level-0 only), category-banner + category-banner-cta on Catalog, product-breadcrumb on ProductDetail. Product-count baseline: 100 products (was 104 pre-iteration; discrepancy predates this run — likely main-agent smoke test residue, no TEST_ product left).
